samples.summary: Two unrelated changes bundled in one PR: an OAuth loopback-binding (nonce/state) security fix across backend+CLI, and the #661 error-envelope `command` attribution refactor touching ~20 CLI files. Neither depends on the other, and the design docs for each land in different sections (cli.md "Login flow" / rest-api.md "CLI Auth" vs cli.md §9). If the originating issue is #661 (as every test comment cites), the auth change is unrequested scope; if it is the auth issue, the envelope refactor is. Splitting would let each be reviewed and reverted independently.
samples.evidence: login.ts adds nonce minting; formatter.ts adds errorEnvelope/backendErrorEnvelope; test comments cite "#661" only for the envelope work.

samples.summary: docs/design/cli.md §9 now asserts "Every emitter builds it through `errorEnvelope` / `backendErrorEnvelope` … so 'one line, attributed' holds", but several CLI error paths still emit bare, unstructured text and bypass the envelope entirely: `login` (`console.error('Token exchange failed…')` L73, `'Failed to fetch user info.'` L90, `Failed to fetch workspaces…` L107, each followed by `process.exit(1)`) and `ctx switch` (`'Not logged in…'` L61, `Workspace not found: …` L67). The doc's universal claim is therefore not satisfied by the implementation — either narrow the claim to the enumerated paths or convert these emitters too.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:73,90,107; packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:61,67 emit plain strings, not JSON envelopes.

samples.summary: §9 now states "A backend error body keeps its `code` and any extra context — agents branch on it", but only the content/export/import/upload/download paths run the backend body through `backendErrorEnvelope`. Every ordinary command (`docs get/create/update/delete`, `notes`, `slides`, `cells`, `tabs`, `api-keys`, `files list/…`) still does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status)`, so the backend `code` is discarded and the envelope reports `"ERROR"`. The doc reads as a global guarantee the code does not provide.
samples.evidence: e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:27, docs.ts:110, notes.ts:70 all `throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)` before reaching outputError.

samples.summary: Version skew is unaddressed and undocumented: a new CLI now hard-requires `state` on its callback, but an older backend (self-hosted, per README `login --server https://api.example.com`) will not echo a nonce. In that pairing every genuine callback is answered 400 and the user gets only the generic 30s "Login timed out" message with no hint of the cause. Neither cli.md's login section nor rest-api.md records a compatibility/rollout note for this (cli.md's Risks table only aspirationally mentions a startup API-compatibility check).
samples.evidence: backend echoes `state` only when `state.nonce` is set (auth.controller.ts:127-131); CLI rejects any callback without a matching state (login.ts nonceMatches gate).

samples.summary: The store already mints a per-flow secret (`csrf`, documented in rest-api.md as the CSRF token embedded in the OAuth state) that is never read or validated anywhere in the backend; this change adds a second per-flow secret (`nonce`) beside it rather than reconciling the two. rest-api.md still describes the CSRF token as a live mechanism while the new paragraph describes the nonce as "what binds a callback to the flow that started it", leaving two overlapping, partly-fictional bindings in the design doc.
samples.evidence: grep for `csrf` in packages/backend/src matches only cli-auth.store.ts and its spec — no consumer.

samples.summary: §8.1's error example is still pretty-printed multi-line JSON while §9 (and this change) mandate a single line on stderr; the shipped skill docs (`packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:57`, `docs-read-content.md:86`) likewise show envelopes without `command`. Harmless illustration-vs-spec drift, but agents are pointed at those files as the contract.
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:782-790 pretty-printed block vs :1029 "a single JSON line on stderr".

finding.summary: Two unrelated changes bundled in one PR: an OAuth loopback-binding (nonce/state) security fix across backend+CLI, and the #661 error-envelope `command` attribution refactor touching ~20 CLI files. Neither depends on the other, and the design docs for each land in different sections (cli.md "Login flow" / rest-api.md "CLI Auth" vs cli.md §9). If the originating issue is #661 (as every test comment cites), the auth change is unrequested scope; if it is the auth issue, the envelope refactor is. Splitting would let each be reviewed and reverted independently.
finding.evidence: login.ts adds nonce minting; formatter.ts adds errorEnvelope/backendErrorEnvelope; test comments cite "#661" only for the envelope work.

verdict.reason: All of the finding's claimed evidence checks out against the tree. login.ts:42-46 mints a 32-byte nonce and sends it with the OAuth start; login.ts:163-210 adds constant-time nonceMatches and the `state` gate in startCallbackServer. formatter.ts:58-135 independently adds commandPath/errorEnvelope/backendErrorEnvelope and the `command` parameter on outputError. The correctness lane's summary (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:3) confirms both workstreams are in the same change set. The only originating-issue artifact in the repo is #661 (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:3), whose Plan and "Acceptance criteria (from the issue)" (lines 26-47) are envelope-only and never mention OAuth, nonces, loopback binding, or `state`; its scope note (lines 19-22) is in fact explicitly narrowing. A grep across all of docs/tasks for nonce|loopback|RFC 8252 finds no task doc for the auth work, so it has no recorded originating issue. Test attribution matches: output.test.ts:153,221,436,466 cite #661 while login-callback.test.ts:4-8 cites only RFC 8252. Docs land in separate sections (cli.md:175-210 Login flow + rest-api.md vs cli.md §9). No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, nothing guards it, and unrequested scope creep is explicitly in the design-fit lane with major severity for failing/exceeding the issue's stated criteria.

finding.summary: docs/design/cli.md §9 now asserts "Every emitter builds it through `errorEnvelope` / `backendErrorEnvelope` … so 'one line, attributed' holds", but several CLI error paths still emit bare, unstructured text and bypass the envelope entirely: `login` (`console.error('Token exchange failed…')` L73, `'Failed to fetch user info.'` L90, `Failed to fetch workspaces…` L107, each followed by `process.exit(1)`) and `ctx switch` (`'Not logged in…'` L61, `Workspace not found: …` L67). The doc's universal claim is therefore not satisfied by the implementation — either narrow the claim to the enumerated paths or convert these emitters too.
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:73,90,107; packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:61,67 emit plain strings, not JSON envelopes.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is that docs/design/cli.md §9 makes an unqualified universal claim that every CLI error path emits the envelope. The doc does not: at docs/design/cli.md:1035-1039 the guarantee sentence is explicitly narrowed — "so 'one line, attributed' holds **on the paths that never throw either: the import/upload/download orchestrators, the backend-error passthroughs on docs/notes/slides content and export, and schema's lookup miss**." The reviewer's quoted ellipsis elides exactly that qualifier. The narrowing the finding asks for ("either narrow the claim to the enumerated paths or convert these emitters too") is already present, and the same enumeration is mirrored in the code comment at packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:66-74. The cited code facts are accurate (login.ts:73,90,107 and ctx.ts:61,67 do emit plain strings), but those paths emit no envelope at all and are outside the doc's enumerated set, so no doc/implementation mismatch exists. Residual: cli.md:1029-1034 states the general "single JSON line on stderr" convention without qualification, so login/ctx remain stylistically inconsistent with the broader convention — but that is a pre-existing interactive-command carve-out, not the specific universal claim this finding attacks, and does not fail a stated acceptance criterion.

finding.summary: Version skew is unaddressed and undocumented: a new CLI now hard-requires `state` on its callback, but an older backend (self-hosted, per README `login --server https://api.example.com`) will not echo a nonce. In that pairing every genuine callback is answered 400 and the user gets only the generic 30s "Login timed out" message with no hint of the cause. Neither cli.md's login section nor rest-api.md records a compatibility/rollout note for this (cli.md's Risks table only aspirationally mentions a startup API-compatibility check).
finding.evidence: backend echoes `state` only when `state.nonce` is set (auth.controller.ts:127-131); CLI rejects any callback without a matching state (login.ts nonceMatches gate).

verdict.reason: The mechanics the finding describes are real (auth.controller.ts:130-134 echoes `state` only when a nonce was stored; login.ts:206-210 400s any callback without a matching state, leaving only the generic 30s timeout at login.ts:257-265), and I confirmed no explicit new-CLI/old-backend rollout paragraph exists in docs/design, packages/documentation, packages/cli/README.md or docs/tasks. However it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. The design-doc discipline requirement is met: the change updated the canonical subsystem docs in place rather than adding a parallel file — docs/design/cli.md:196-210 documents the nonce binding and explicitly that a mismatched callback is "answered 400 and ignored", and docs/design/rest-api.md:334-345 documents the backend surface including that the nonce is optional. All sections required by docs/design/template.md:10-31 are present, and cli.md's Risks table already carries the CLI/API version-drift row (cli.md:1080). No Non-Goal (cli.md:55-77) is exceeded, no existing module is duplicated, and the finding cites no acceptance criterion it fails — it argues from the absence of a polish-level compatibility note, which is a documentation preference (minor, never blocking). The remaining substance — that a stale-backend pairing surfaces only a generic timeout with no diagnostic — is an error-diagnostics/robustness concern in the correctness lens's lane, not spec-conformance, and is in fact already logged there (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:8).

finding.summary: Scope creep: the PR converts the hand-rolled error emitters the issue's own task plan explicitly deferred. The plan's Scope note (lines 19–22) says the forwarded upstream bodies in `docs.ts`/`slides.ts`/`notes.ts`, `src/docs/import.ts`, `src/files/*` and `schema.ts` "are the subject of #654/#655 and are left alone here", yet this diff rewrites every one of them through the new `backendErrorEnvelope`/`errorEnvelope` builders (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202, notes.ts:155, slides.ts:161, schema.ts:40, files/upload.ts, files/download.ts, docs/import.ts, notes/import.ts, slides/import.ts). Either the scope note should be updated in this PR (it was not) or the work belongs in #654/#655, where it now risks duplicating/conflicting with in-flight work. The #661 acceptance criteria (single line, `command`, unchanged code/message) are satisfied by the `outputError` change alone.
finding.evidence: todo.md:19-22 "Scope note: … Hand-rolled emitters that bypass `outputError` (…) are the subject of #654/#655 and are left alone here." vs. diff converting all of them.

verdict.reason: The scope note exists exactly as quoted (todo.md:19-22) and reserves the hand-rolled emitters in docs.ts/slides.ts/notes.ts, src/docs/import.ts, src/files/*, and schema.ts for #654/#655, while the todo's Plan (lines 26-38) limits the work to formatter.ts, commandPath, threading `this` at outputError call sites, cli.ts preAction, and tests. The tree shows every one of those deferred emitters converted to the new shared builders: docs.ts:203/269, notes.ts:156/217, slides.ts:162/219, schema.ts:41, files/upload.ts:148-229, files/download.ts:64, docs/import.ts:146-276, notes/import.ts:134-220, slides/import.ts:160-328. formatter.ts:66-114 explicitly documents this broader remit and docs/design/cli.md:1035-1042 was updated to claim "Every emitter builds it through errorEnvelope / backendErrorEnvelope", yet the task doc's scope note was left stale and now contradicts the diff it ships with. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, nothing renders it unreachable, and scope expansion past an explicitly deferred boundary is within the design-fit lens (major = exceeds a stated non-goal / unrequested scope creep). The stated acceptance criteria (single line, `command`, unchanged code/message) concern the outputError envelope, so the extra conversions are not plainly compelled by them.

finding.summary: An unrelated feature is bundled into an error-envelope PR: the OAuth callback nonce/state binding (CLI `login.ts`, backend `github-auth.guard.ts`, `cli-auth.store.ts`, `auth.controller.ts`, plus cli.md/rest-api.md login sections). Nothing in issue #661's outcome or acceptance criteria (single-line envelope + `command` attribution) covers CLI login security. Mixing a protocol/security change with an output-formatting change makes the PR reviewable only as two changes and couples their revert.
finding.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md lists only formatter/call-site/test work; the diff also adds nonce minting, backend storage and echo.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:42-46` mints a 32-byte nonce and appends `&nonce=` to the OAuth start URL; `login.ts:163-210` adds constant-time `state` validation in `startCallbackServer`. Backend counterparts exist in `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts`, `cli-auth.store.ts`, and `auth.controller.ts`, with docs written up at `docs/design/cli.md:175-205` (and `docs/design/rest-api.md`). Meanwhile the originating task doc `docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md` (Issue #661) scopes the work to `formatter.ts` single-line output, a `commandPath` helper, `outputError(this)` call-site threading, the `cli.ts` preAction hook, and tests; its acceptance criteria (lines 42-47) cover only single-line envelope, `command` attribution, and unchanged `code`/`message`. No active task doc covers CLI OAuth nonce/state binding. Sibling lens summaries (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:3, .agent-review/test-adequacy/summary.md:5) independently describe the nonce plumbing as new in this change ("New nonce plumbing in GitHubAuthGuard", "the CLI now unconditionally requires a state echo"), so it is not pre-existing tree state. Unrequested scope creep relative to the issue's outcome/acceptance is explicitly in the design-fit lane and is a major-kind fit violation, not a taste preference. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, reachable (it is on the default `wafflebase login` path), and in scope for this lens.

searchedFor: grep 'nonce|RFC 8252' across docs/ (only design docs and unrelated archives matched)
finding.summary: No task plan under `docs/tasks/active/` for the OAuth nonce work. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 requires a feature / non-trivial change to have both an updated design doc *and* a task plan (`YYYYMMDD-<slug>-todo.md` with a paired `-lessons.md`). The design docs (cli.md login flow, rest-api.md CLI Auth) were updated, but no todo/lessons pair exists for the nonce change; the only active CLI task doc is the #661 envelope one, whose plan does not mention login at all.
finding.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 'Feature / non-trivial change → write or update a design doc … → create a task plan under docs/tasks/active/'.

verdict.reason: The cited requirement is real and accurately quoted: CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 (reinforced at :60-63 and CLAUDE.md:58-61) requires a non-trivial change to have both an updated design doc and a paired task plan under docs/tasks/active/ (YYYYMMDD-<slug>-todo.md + -lessons.md). The nonce/state-binding work is a login-protocol change (docs/design/cli.md:196-205 documents the new binding; packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts and packages/backend/src/auth/* implement it), so the task-plan path applies. I searched for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide `grep -i nonce` returns 17 files, none under docs/tasks; `grep -i nonce` over all 843 files in docs/tasks (active + archive) returns nothing; keyword greps for loopback/csrf/timingSafeEqual/cli-exchange/127.0.0.1 in docs/tasks surface only the archived 20260315-cli-oauth-login-todo.md, which describes the pre-nonce flow (plain `?code=` redirect, no state echo); the full 37-entry docs/tasks/active listing has no login/OAuth slug, and the only CLI task pair (20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md/-lessons.md) is scoped strictly to issue #661's error envelope and never mentions login, nonce, or state. Neither docs/tasks/README.md nor docs/tasks/active/README.md exempts security fixes from the paired-file rule, so there is no "already-guarded" ground either. Absence stands.
